title: Deeper/broader cross-language DXF codec and consumer-claim consistency review
mode: Primary project documentation, source, and issue review; research-only plan refinement
scope: Extend the DXF peer screen to the IxMilia Rust DXF/DXB implementation and map current issue reports to existing local owners.
Reconcile FreeCAD's generic no-loss interchange wording with its documented importer-specific entity and ACIS limits.
Recheck the BRL-CAD polyface proposal and preserve the existing signed-index and direct-wire local test contract.
Refine only optional composed-checkpoint comparator selection; preserve implementation speed, fixture policy, and validation cadence.

method.kind: Read-only review of primary project documentation, source, and issue pages
method.limitations: GitHub issue reports are not independently reproduced and some lack a hash-bound attachment. Mutable repository/docs pages and API type declarations do not prove runtime behavior, native acceptance, or 3D semantics. No peer route was executed.

sources.observed: The Rust project reads/writes DXF and DXB but not DWG. Its docs list typed Solid3D, Region, and Body APIs; its README says ODA File Converter interop tests are Windows-only and optional. The reviewed open reports concern polyface vertex group-70 output, a SURFACE not appearing in a reported entity inventory, suspected zero/duplicate APPID handle AutoCAD rejection, NaN lexical parsing, and timezone-dependent save panic in crate 0.6.0.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Mutable source/docs and unverified issue reports; typed API presence and same-codec/ODA conversion tests do not prove ACIS semantics or native AutoCAD acceptance. No issue establishes a libdxfrw defect.

sources.project: IxMilia .NET DXF and Rust DXF lineage
sources.observed: The C# and Rust repositories are distinct implementations within the same author/organization family; the .NET README itself cautions that some 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY writer output may not open in AutoCAD.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Separate code paths may be compared for runtime-specific behavior, but should not be treated as independent authorship/specification votes.

sources.observed: The documentation describes separate importer subsets, stock inability to read embedded ACIS/SAT solids, and a DWG converter-to-DXF-to-selected-importer pipeline. A generic no-loss DXF/DWG interchange assertion is inconsistent with those route-specific limitations.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Documentation consistency and intended route only; not native Linux/Windows qualification or evidence for an arbitrary FreeCAD build/importer selection.

sources.observed: The proposed #245 guard remains open and uses positive-only polyface index checks, while the documented DXF contract uses signed indices for invisible edges and zero as the active-list terminator. The local writer's direct ASCII/Binary group-70 regression already checks coordinate flags 192 and face flags 128.
sources.evidenceCeiling: A peer proposal and specification cross-check; not a reason to import peer code, run malformed peer cases, or reopen the already-tested local wire rule.

existingOwners: PAR-20 MATERIAL graph and payload implementation
assessment.planEffect: Add the Rust DXF/DXB route and issue evidence as optional, artifact-pinned comparator context; prefer exact importer profiles over FreeCAD's generic no-loss statement; retain the completed local polyface raw-wire assertion and current implementation order.
